name: Supravalvular Aortic Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Supravalvular Aortic Stenosis

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of localized narrowing of the ascending aorta above the aortic valve
Presence of a systolic ejection murmur best heard at the right upper sternal border
Identification of pathogenic mutation or deletion in the ELN gene
Imaging evidence of stenosis in other large arteries (e.g., pulmonary artery, coronary arteries)
Presence of facial dysmorphisms or features suggestive of Williams syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of supravalvular aortic narrowing plus clinical murmur; genetic testing supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by cardiac catheterization and angiography if echocardiography is inconclusive.

laboratory: Elevated serum calcium in some cases associated with Williams syndrome
imaging: Echocardiogram showing supravalvular aortic narrowing and left ventricular hypertrophy
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography demonstrating extent of arterial stenosis
Cardiac catheterization with pressure gradient measurement across stenosis
other: Physical exam revealing characteristic systolic murmur

distinguishingFeatures: Narrowing occurs at the aortic valve rather than above it
Obstruction located below the aortic valve
Presence of subaortic membrane or muscular ridge on imaging
Narrowing typically distal to the left subclavian artery
Upper limb hypertension with lower limb hypotension

redFlags: Severe left ventricular hypertrophy with heart failure symptoms
Progressive angina indicating coronary artery involvement
references: Miller DT, et al. Supravalvular Aortic Stenosis. GeneReviews. 2020.
Williams syndrome and supravalvular aortic stenosis: clinical and molecular insights. Circulation. 2018.
Diagnosis and management of supravalvular aortic stenosis. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2019.
